name: Quinn Fong
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember an eye test using letters I knew by heart.” People around Breakwater Way know Quinn by a small Saturday habit. Quinn stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I can't see the maker's mark. My granddaughter read it out and found her own middle name.
appearance: Quinn is easy to recognize by a long silver braid and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in a cream pullover with one cuff folded back twice, Quinn gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Quinn loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To identify the maker with the granddaughter.
family: Jean Miranda is Quinn’s cousin’s child. Quinn picks the meeting place. Jean sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Jean says, “I sharpen pencils for class because it gives my shaking hands a job.”
connections: Aidan Hayward. The maker's name finally goes beside the old haircut bought with fish.
